audit.title: Request Computation (Chainlink Functions: Simple Computation)

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Opens well — "This tutorial shows you how to run computations on the Chainlink Functions DON." Weak spot: `### FunctionsConsumerExample.sol` is an empty heading with no liftable content beneath it.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong hierarchy — 7 headings, 1 H1, 0 level skips, no section over 600 words. Weakness: the encoding-helper functions are a bulleted list that would extract better as a table; one heading is empty.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Strong — real fulfillment cost `0.240613623834519812 LINK`, gas/router/DON identifiers, hex response strings, decoded `453`. 21 prose numerals plus 22 in code.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Strong; no action needed. 18 links, 7 to primary sources (GitHub source files, functions-toolkit README, Remix contract).

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Encoding-helper descriptions are crisply liftable ("Takes a positive JavaScript integer number and returns a Buffer of 32 bytes representing a uint256 type"). But no self-contained definition of "Chainlink Functions" or "DON" near first use.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak. Measured facts confirm 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified, 0 og/twitter tags. Code fences are all correctly language-tagged, which helps.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Mixed. The run command and full simulated output are excellent and copy-pasteable, but `source.js` and `request.js` are only linked to GitHub — an agent must fetch external files to see the actual code. 2 blocks contain placeholder comments.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Covers setup → run → examine. Missing: no troubleshooting/FAQ, no error-string coverage (e.g., "secp256k1 unavailable", simulation failures, fulfillment code errors).

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Clean and consistent. Minor typo: "access theses values."

audit.summary: This is a clean, well-linked Chainlink Functions tutorial that walks through running a geometric-mean computation on the DON, with strong concrete specifics (real costs, addresses, hex outputs) and heavy primary-source linking (7 GitHub/Remix references). Its single biggest strength is verifiable specificity — actual transaction hashes and LINK costs make claims attributable. Its single biggest opportunity is machine-readability: no JSON-LD, no canonical URL, and no freshness dates were served, which weakens agent trust and E-E-A-T signaling. An empty `### FunctionsConsumerExample.sol` heading and code that lives only on GitHub (not inline) also cost retrieval and runnability points. Note: the page carries a `shutdown` callout — a relevance/freshness flag that should be reflected in a visible dated status.

recommendations.title: Add TechArticle JSON-LD, canonical URL, and visible last-updated date
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified`, `programmingLanguage: JavaScript`, a self-referential `canonical`, and add a visible "Last updated" line. Confirm the CLI passes raw `<head>` — if the site templates this, verify server-side rendering.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and freshness signals are what agents parse to establish trust and recency; their absence caps E-E-A-T scoring.

recommendations.title: Fill or remove the empty `FunctionsConsumerExample.sol` heading
recommendations.issue: Heading has zero content beneath it
recommendations.change: Either inline the consumer contract (with `sendRequest`/`fulfillRequest` shown) or delete the heading. An empty heading produces a null RAG chunk that can be retrieved and returned as an incomplete answer.
recommendations.why: Empty sections degrade chunk quality and answer-first extraction; every heading should open with a self-contained answer.

recommendations.title: Inline the core of `source.js` and `request.js`
recommendations.issue: "The code is self-explanatory" — but the code is only on GitHub
recommendations.change: Embed the geometric-mean computation and the `makeRequestSepolia` skeleton (imports, `simulateScript`, `SubscriptionManager`, `sendRequest`, `ResponseListener`) as tagged, copy-pasteable blocks with the router/donId values shown.
recommendations.why: Agents completing tasks cannot follow external links reliably; inline complete snippets are directly liftable and executable.

recommendations.title: Add a symptom-phrased Troubleshooting section
recommendations.issue: No error/symptom coverage; devs query by error string
recommendations.change: Add H3s phrased as observed messages/questions: "secp256k1 unavailable, reverting to browser version", "Simulation failed", "Why is my fulfillmentCode not 0?", "Request not fulfilled after five minutes". Answer each in the first sentence.
recommendations.why: Symptom-phrased headings win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses, even when the fix is in body text.

recommendations.title: Convert the encoding-helper list to a table
recommendations.issue: Three parallel helper descriptions in prose bullets (0 tables on page)
recommendations.change: Make a 3-column table: Helper | Input type | Solidity output type. Add `encodeBytes`/`encodeString` variants if applicable.
recommendations.why: Tables let engines extract structured comparisons and pick the right helper for a stated return type.

recommendations.title: Add a leading one-sentence canonical definition
recommendations.issue: "DON" and "Chainlink Functions" used before a crisp definition
recommendations.change: Add: "Chainlink Functions is a serverless platform that runs your JavaScript on a Decentralized Oracle Network (DON) and returns the result onchain to your smart contract."
recommendations.why: A self-contained definition near first use is verbatim-liftable and defends against generic parametric substitution.

recommendations.title: Fix typo "theses values"
recommendations.why: Clean prose is independently rewarded; typos reduce fluency signals.

antiPatterns: Empty heading `### FunctionsConsumerExample.sol` — produces a null retrievable chunk.
"The code is self-explanatory" x2 — defers to external files the reader/agent may not fetch; not a substitute for inline code.
No visible date on a page carrying a `shutdown` product callout — status ambiguity for freshness-sensitive readers.
No keyword stuffing or marketing fluff observed.
offPageNotes: The page references `/llms.txt` — good site-level signal; confirm it lists this URL.
Site-level JSON-LD/canonical templating may exist but was not served here; verify rendered `<head>` output rather than assuming absence.
The `shutdown` callout suggests product deprecation — a site-level content-lifecycle decision (archive vs. redirect) that affects long-term retrieval value beyond this page's control.
